title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a locked adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced a shared initial candidate and a guarded final artifact after validator + repair when invoked. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute reduction = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported. The single discordant improvement (baseline-invalid → guarded-valid) is archived in the run artifacts (see Methods and Disclosure). Because residual guarded failures = 0, the preregistered secondary hypothesis comparing residual error-type proportions is not testable and any error-type discussion is exploratory. We correct inconsistent discordant-labeling in the original draft, clarify provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair), and point auditors to the exact artifact files and SHA-256 checksums for forensic inspection.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are proposed for intent-driven network operations (NetOps) such as translating human intent into vendor-specific configurations. Operational deployment proposals often add deterministic validators and automated repair steps as guardrails, but rigorous, preregistered evidence quantifying the practical reduction in actionable misconfiguration under controlled conditions is scarce. Research question. After an autonomy-locked preregistration, we asked: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types remain after automated repairs? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001) executed end-to-end with archived synthetic tasks and a deterministic validator; (2) complete artifact release and cryptographic hashes; (3) an artifact-grounded null/near-null confirmatory result for the chosen model/validator/task bank; (4) explicit corrections and clarifications requested during peer review (discordant-cell labeling, provider-call accounting, and the untestability of H2).
sections.related_work: Prior work motivates guarded generate→validate→repair pipelines and deterministic validators for NetOps (e.g., header-space analysis and incremental checkers). Representative verified sources used for positioning and method design include: Kazemian et al. (Header Space Analysis) and Khurshid et al. (VeriFlow/NetPlumber), and recent NetOps→LLM evaluation prototypes (NetConfEval). We used verified literature for gap identification and to justify a focused confirmatory test of the marginal benefit of deterministic validation + single automated repair under a paired design.
sections.methodology: Preregistration. The study plan (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001, preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815ea...) was frozen before execution. Design and estimand. Paired binary design on N=200 independent synthetic intent→configuration tasks stratified across three vendor families; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary hypothesis H1 (confirmatory): guarded pipeline reduces final actionable misconfiguration rate by ≥50% relative to initial LLM-only outputs. Secondary hypothesis H2 (confirmatory): residual guarded errors are more likely semantic/policy than syntactic. Execution contract and model. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Budgeted maximum model calls = 400; actual model_calls_used = 201 (recorded in execution manifest). Generation semantics. The preregistered contract used a shared_initial_candidate per task (independent_condition_generation = false); baseline and guarded conditions both reference that shared initial candidate. Repair policy. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task; across the run exactly one repair invocation occurred (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1; condition_counts: shared = 200, guarded = 1; see deterministic reconciliation). Validator and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applied full intent-constraint validation and simulator-based semantic checks. Each task produced machine-readable per-task scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ and an entry in execution/raw_results.jsonl (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). Missingness, retries, and exclusions followed the preregistered plan; no model-call failures occurred and complete pairs = 200.
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 on archived scoring JSONs. Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline_success_count = 199 (baseline success rate = 0.995). Guarded_success_count = 200 (guarded success rate = 1.000). Paired absolute reduction (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Discordant-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Note the corrected interpretation: the single discordant observation is baseline-invalid → guarded-valid (n_10 = 1), i.e., one task was initially scored invalid and after the adapter's single repair the guarded outcome was valid. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the absolute reduction = [0.0, 0.015] (bootstrap resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). Secondary outcomes and hypothesis H2. Because residual guarded actionable failures = 0 (n_00 + n_01 = 0), the preregistered confirmatory contingency test for H2 (residual error-type proportions) is not executable; any inference about residual error-type prevalence is therefore exploratory and constrained by the absence of guarded failures. Forensic artifact pointer for the discordant case. The discordant episode is recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 above) and in the per-pair contingency file analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 above). The full per-task scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/; auditors may locate the specific scoring JSON for the discordant pair by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 above) for the entry with guarded=1 and baseline=0 and then inspecting the referenced execution/scoring/<episode>-baseline.json and execution/scoring/<episode>-guarded.json entries. Deterministic accounting. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, provider_call_audit.hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, condition_counts = {"shared": 200, "guarded": 1} (deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f82604...).
sections.discussion: Interpretation. Under the constrained experimental conditions (synthetic task bank, single hosted model gpt-5-mini, a single deterministic validator implementation, and the adapter-enforced single-repair budget), the guarded pipeline yielded only a numerically small absolute reduction because the baseline LLM-generated actionable-error prevalence was already very low (1/200). Operational implications. Deterministic validators remain important for canonicalization, auditing, and catching systematic classes of errors; however, the operational ROI (reduced human review, reduced outages) depends on baseline generator accuracy, validator coverage, repair budget, and human-in-the-loop costs. Study limitations that affect interpretation. (a) Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; no multi-model generality is implied. (b) Synthetic benchmark scope and validator semantics: task realism and validator coverage bound external validity. (c) Low baseline error prevalence: only one baseline failure limits power to detect moderate relative improvements and makes effect-size estimates imprecise for rarer failure regimes. (d) Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract limited repair to one call per task; multi-attempt repair regimes are unexplored here. (e) Secondary hypothesis untestable: because guarded residual failures = 0 we could not run the preregistered confirmatory contingency test for H2; this is reported transparently and moved to exploratory status. Auditability and reproducibility. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts referenced above are archived with SHA-256 checksums (preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815ea..., execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8..., analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2..., deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). These artifacts support independent verification of the corrected discordant labeling, provider-call accounting, and per-task traces.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory study of a deterministic-validator guard for LLM→NetOps generate→verify→repair pipelines. On the selected synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator/repair adapter (≤1 repair), the absolute actionable-misconfiguration reduction was 0.005 (from 1/200 to 0/200). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction) is not supported by the data. We correct prior discordant-cell mislabeling (the single discordant pair is baseline-invalid → guarded-valid), clarify provider-call accounting (model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair), and explicitly report that H2 was untestable due to zero guarded residual failures. All artifacts and cryptographic hashes required for forensic audit are archived as described in the Disclosure Statement. Future work should expand model coverage, validator implementations, repair budgets, and task realism to map operational regimes in which validator-assisted repair materially reduces actionable risk.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to real production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage gaps or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.
